v01_progress_ladder.title: Progress ladder
v01_progress_ladder.what: Start and end prevalence for stunting, underweight, and stunting by sex.
v01_progress_ladder.why: Shows the size of progress in one glance: stunting fell 35.4 points and underweight 38.9 points between 1990 and 2019.

v02_pace_forest.title: Pace of decline (forest plot)
v02_pace_forest.what: Average annual reduction with 95% intervals, overall and by period.
v02_pace_forest.why: Compares methods and periods on one scale: the robust slope (3.1%) agrees with the main fit (3.02%), and the later period (3.59%) is faster but its interval overlaps.

v03_projection_fan.title: Projection sensitivity (fan)
v03_projection_fan.what: 26 trend lines (start years 1986–2011) projected to 2030, with observed values and the reference level.
v03_projection_fan.why: Shows how fragile a single projection is: the 2025 trend value ranges from 21.7% to 26.0% depending on the start year, so planning should use the range.

v04_epidemic_calendar.title: Epidemic calendar
v04_epidemic_calendar.what: Weekly cases laid out by year and ISO week.
v04_epidemic_calendar.why: Makes timing and repeat patterns visible: the major waves (peaks 2020-06-28, 2021-04-11, 2021-08-01, 2022-01-30, 2022-07-03) do not follow a fixed season.

v05_south_asia_small_multiples.title: South Asia small multiples
v05_south_asia_small_multiples.what: Weekly reported cases per million for eight countries, one panel each.
v05_south_asia_small_multiples.why: Puts Bangladesh's curve in regional context on a population-fair scale: its busiest week reached 608 cases per million, against 1,983 for India and 2,071 for Nepal (differences also reflect testing).

v06_case_death_lag.title: Case-to-death lag
v06_case_death_lag.what: Correlation between weekly growth in cases and growth in deaths at lags of 0–8 weeks.
v06_case_death_lag.why: Checks how quickly deaths respond to cases: the strongest link is at 1 week (r = 0.61); the fatality ratio in this project assumes a 2-week lag, so treat it as an approximation.

v07_division_month_heatmap.title: Division-by-month heatmap
v07_division_month_heatmap.what: Mean monthly cases per 100,000 population for each division and month.
v07_division_month_heatmap.why: Shows the season and the geography together: the highest average month is Oct in Dhaka, and nearly all divisions are quiet from January to May.

v08_seasonal_clock.title: Seasonal clock
v08_seasonal_clock.what: Share of all reported cases falling in each calendar month.
v08_seasonal_clock.why: Tells programmes when to be ready: September–November holds 64% of cases, with October the peak at 25.7%.

v09_division_streamgraph.title: Division streamgraph
v09_division_streamgraph.what: Monthly cases for each division, stacked symmetrically around a centre line.
v09_division_streamgraph.why: Shows how national peaks are built: Dhaka supplies most of the volume, but other divisions swell in the same months; the single peak month was September 2023 (79,598 cases).

v10_burden_vs_severity.title: Burden vs severity
v10_burden_vs_severity.what: Division incidence against case fatality, sized by deaths.
v10_burden_vs_severity.why: Separates 'many cases' from 'many deaths': Dhaka has 717 cases per 100,000 and 0.63% fatality, Barishal a similar incidence (766) but lower fatality (0.45%); Dhaka's deaths may include patients referred from elsewhere.
